//: Type checking for the JavaScript that is already here.  Nothing is compiled and no file is renamed: `tsc --noEmit`
reads the JSDoc the codebase has written all along (4,690 @param and 2,319 @returns at the time this was added) and
says where it does not match what the code does.  `npm test` runs it.
Scope is shared/ and server/ — the code every game depends on.  The sixteen game modules and the client are not in
it, deliberately: typing them is a far larger job (164 .vue files, and the room bags that each game extends with its
own fields), and it would have to wait for its own decision rather than riding along with this one.
The tests are left out.  They pass malformed input on purpose — that is most of what shared/leaks.js and the fuzz
tests are for — so checking them would report that deliberate nonsense as hundreds of errors and drown the rest.
`strict` is off.  Turning it on is a separate, larger piece of work: it is mostly strictNullChecks, which this code
answers with `??` and early returns rather than with types, and it would multiply the count several times over.
